FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk AND p.p_channel_tv = 'N'
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query spends most time scanning the store_sales table to find rows where ss_customer_sk IS NULL, which likely reads a large volume of data from S3. The subsequent broadcast join and aggregations are lightweight because the promotion table is tiny (300 rows).

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on … and p.p_channel_tv = ')
The scan of store_sales with pushed filter IsNull(ss_customer_sk) still reads a significant fraction of the table because many rows have null ss_customer_sk, making I/O the dominant cost.

The left outer broadcast hash join processes every filtered store_sales row; if the filtered dataset is large, the CPU cost of probing the broadcasted promotion hash table could be non-trivial despite the small build side.

The partial hash aggregate (counting per partition) adds overhead of serialization and the subsequent single-partition exchange (node 11) if the number of partitions is high, though this is usually minor compared to the scan.
